title: An abstract set annotation hands back a mutable set
text_original: Potentially breaking: Abstract sets are now structured into frozensets. This allows hashability, better immutability and is more consistent with the collections.abc.Set type. See Migrations for steps to restore legacy behavior.
text_rewritten: We annotate read-only set-shaped fields with the abstract set type because callers must not mutate them, and the models holding them are used as dictionary keys. Structuring hands back a mutable set, so the model is unhashable and the field can be mutated behind our back. The abstract annotation should produce an immutable, hashable set - a frozenset - while the mutable-set annotation and the built-in set type keep producing mutable sets and the built-in frozenset type keeps behaving as it does. This should hold for a bare call, for a field inside a model, and on both shipped converters.

acceptance_hint: Structuring against an abstract set annotation yields a hashable frozenset with the elements converted as before, while mutable-set and built-in set annotations still yield mutable sets.
